create.name: Peter Russell
create.bio:
Peter Russell is a British writer and teacher on consciousness and meditation. He read mathematics and theoretical physics at Cambridge before switching to experimental psychology, then spent time in India learning meditation and Eastern thought; back in England he held what he describes as Britain's first research post on the psychology of meditation. For two decades he ran courses for businesses on creativity and personal development, and in 1982 his book The Global Brain coined that phrase and anticipated a connected planet. He teaches as part of the Institute of Noetic Sciences faculty and is a fellow of the Findhorn Foundation.

His teaching today centres on effortless meditation: the idea that the mind settles most easily when we stop trying to make it quiet, and that letting go is closer to letting be than to pushing anything away. He offers this through a five-week online audio course priced on a pay-what-you-wish basis, a series of online talks, private consultations by phone, and short guided practices on his long-running website, The Spirit of Now. Among his books are Letting Go of Nothing and From Science to God, as well as Waking Up in Time and a guide to effortless meditation.

books.title: How to Meditate Without Even Trying
books.author: Peter Russell
books.description: A short guide to his effortless approach. It shows how easing off effort, relaxing attention and gently coming back to the present lets meditation happen on its own, for beginners and practised meditators alike.

books.title: Letting Go of Nothing: Relax Your Mind and Discover the Wonder of Your True Nature
books.author: Peter Russell
books.description: Treats letting go less as dropping things and more as letting them be. He applies this to judgements, fears, attachments and fixed beliefs, with short reflections and practices; Eckhart Tolle wrote the foreword.

books.title: Forgiving Humanity: How the Most Innovative Species Became the Most Dangerous
books.author: Peter Russell
books.description: A reflection on why accelerating change has made our species a danger to itself, and on how inner change and self-understanding might help us respond with compassion rather than blame.

courses.title: How to Meditate Without Even Trying (online course)
courses.description: A five-week audio course sent one lesson a week, each a short talk followed by a guided meditation of about twenty minutes. It moves from simple present-moment practice to his later, more effortless techniques, and you choose what to pay.

courses.title: Private consultations
courses.description: One-to-one conversations, usually by phone, on meditation practice, questions around spiritual awakening and consciousness, and creative thinking about personal challenges.

free_resources.title: Meditation for Air Travellers
free_resources.description: A free guided meditation from his site, made to download and listen to while flying.

free_resources.title: Meditation tips and free guided meditations
free_resources.description: His meditation hub page, with short tips on common difficulties, a three-minute guided meditation and other free recordings including a forgiveness practice and nondual vipassana.
